'''Sports'''
*[[2025–26 UEFA Champions League]]
**[[2026 UEFA Champions League final]]
***In [[association football]], defending champions [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] (PSG) win their second [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] title after defeating [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] 4–3 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] following a 1–1 draw after [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]] during the final at [[Puskás Aréna]] in [[Budapest]], [[Hungary]]. **[[2026 Paris Saint-Germain celebration riots]]
***Following PSG's Champions League victory, [[Paris Police Prefecture|police]] arrest more than 280 people in [[Paris]], [[France]], following clashes, vandalism, [[arson]], an attempted intrusion into a police station, and disruptions to traffic and [[Transport in Paris|public transport]] during celebrations. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/may/30/paris-police-arrest-paris-saint-germain-fans-celebrate-champions-league-win-over-arsenal (AFP via ''The Guardian'')] [https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/jubilant-psg-supporters-spill-onto-paris-streets-some-clashes-with-police-2026-05-30/ (Reuters)]

**In [[basketball]], the [[San Antonio Spurs]] defeat the [[2025 NBA Finals|defending champions]], the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], in [[List of NBA game sevens|seven games]] to win the [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]] [[NBA conference finals|finals]] and reach the [[2026 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] for the first time since [[2014 NBA Finals|2014]], where they will face the [[New York Knicks]].
